picks.title: Apple’s first smart display is the 7-inch HomeView for $299
picks.excerpt: It can recognize up to six users with its camera.
picks.rationale: This is the one Apple Oct 13 event pick. HomeView is Apple's first smart display, a new device category for Apple, and it uses camera face recognition to personalize Siri AI for up to six people. Pre-orders open at $299.

picks.title: Samsung Smart Glasses Unveiled, and They're Superlight
picks.excerpt: They might be called Galaxy Glasses, and they're coming in November.
picks.rationale: Samsung unveiled its first Android XR AI glasses with a November launch window. It is a reveal, not a leak, and it puts a new major player in the AI-glasses race.

picks.title: Big surprise: Some Ray-Ban Meta owners say their glasses are listening without being asked (Updated)
picks.excerpt: A Ray-Ban Meta owner claims three pairs of smart glasses captured conversations without the "Hey Meta" wake phrase, with other owners reporting unexplained Meta AI activations; Meta says the issue has been resolved.
picks.rationale: This is a new privacy incident: Meta AI on the glasses activated and recorded without the wake phrase. Meta says it has fixed the issue. It is a concrete failure of the always-listening model behind AI wearables.

picks.title: Robots could get a ‘ChatGPT moment’ in the next one to two years, Unitree chief says — and it’ll be powered by OpenAI’s GPT-7
picks.excerpt: Unitree’s CEO believes robotic AI could see a huge ‘ChatGPT moment’ when GPT-7 launches next year.
picks.rationale: This is the robots pick. The CEO of the largest consumer humanoid and robot-dog maker gives a dated forecast for an embodied-AI breakthrough and ties it to OpenAI's GPT-7.

picks.title: Smart ring maker Ultrahuman to roll out biological-age model across UAE
picks.excerpt: Ultrahuman and Abu Dhabi will spend the next two years working on research and clinical validation of the model.
picks.rationale: This is the wearables pick. Ultrahuman and Abu Dhabi will roll out a smart-ring biological-age model and validate it clinically over two years, taking ring data toward health-system use.

alternates.title: XREAL Aura with Android XR start at $1,279
alternates.excerpt: XREAL’s first pair of Android XR glasses, XREAL Aura, finally have a price tag – $1,279. XREAL makes glasses that...
alternates.rationale: Pricing for the first Android XR glasses from XREAL. It would be a third glasses card, so it is an alternate.

alternates.title: Two affordable smart glasses launch, one with 20MP Sony camera, one with tint-shift lenses
alternates.excerpt: Rogbid launched the $139.99 VisionMax with a 20 MP camera and an AI assistant running on Alibaba’s Tongyi Qianwen and GPT-5.4 for object ID, 100-language translation and meeting transcription, plus the $69.99 camera-less VisionShift Pro.
alternates.rationale: Budget AI glasses launch at $139.99. It would be a third glasses card, so it is an alternate.

alternates.title: Spotify users on iOS 27 can now ask Siri to play music without having to say 'on Spotify'
alternates.excerpt: Siri can now learn users' preferred music app, allowing Spotify listeners to request songs, podcasts, and playlists without specifying which app to use.
alternates.rationale: Siri AI now learns your default music app. It is a second Apple-adjacent card and a software feature, so it is an alternate.

https://arstechnica.com/apple/2026/10/ap.new_action: Apple officially launched HomeView at its Oct 13 event, with a $299 price, pre-orders and six-person face recognition. The 09-22 MacRumors card was a rumor and the 10-09 Engadget card (https://www.engadget.com/2281263/apple-is-set-to-show-off-new-smart-home-devices-at-an-october-13-event/) only announced the event. The candidate's history_match (TechRadar robotic monitor arm, 10-09) is unrelated; MacRumors is the closer published story.

https://www.cnet.com/tech/mobile/samsung.new_action: Samsung unveiled the glasses with a November launch. The 10-02 Road to VR card reported only an FCC filing. The candidate's history_match (Wired Galaxy Watch9 review, 09-20) is unrelated; Road to VR is the closer published story.

dedup.note: Apple Oct 13 event treated as one story cluster, with a single pick: Ars Technica HomeView, the strongest AI-device angle (a new category with face-recognition Siri AI). The other 13 event items are dropped as the same story: Wired HomeView x2, Gizmodo HomeView, TechRadar HomeView, Apple Newsroom, 9to5Mac facial recognition and EU, Engadget/CNET/MacRumors/Android Authority on HomePod mini 2 and Apple TV 4K, and 9to5Mac on Siri AI for older Apple TVs. Ray-Ban Meta Audio reviews (Engadget, Tom's Guide; cluster c1) are dropped as the same story as the 10-05 UploadVR Ray-Ban Meta Audio launch card. The Engadget review was tagged likely-repeat against the 10-10 Gizmodo Gen 3 review, a different model, but the launch it reviews was already published. Samsung glasses leaks (9to5Google, SamMobile; cluster c12) are dropped as within-pool duplicates of the CNET reveal, which was kept. Lower priority: Gemini publish-styles teardown (an app teardown, not a gadget) and Motorola Razr AI key (already an alternate on 10-13). XREAL Aura and Rogbid glasses are alternates to avoid a third glasses card. The final 5 come from 5 distinct outlets and cover a smart display, glasses x2, a robot and a ring.
